lines.text: Most states have no lemon law just for used cars.
lines.say: Most states have no lemon law just for used cars.

lines.text: Only about 10 states have one, like New York and Massachusetts.
lines.say: Only about ten states have one, like New York.

lines.text: New cars differ: all 50 states have one. If a substantial defect isn't fixed after repeated tries, the maker must refund or replace it.
lines.say: New cars differ: all fifty states have one. If a substantial defect isn't fixed after repeated tries, the maker must refund or replace it.

lines.text: California, for example, presumes a lemon within 18 months or 18,000 miles: 4 repair tries (maker notified; 2 for safety defects), or over 30 days in the shop.
lines.say: California, for example, presumes a lemon within eighteen months or eighteen thousand miles: four repair tries, two for safety defects, or over thirty days in the shop.

lines.text: Typically not covered: accident damage, abuse or neglect, unauthorized mods, and minor defects.
lines.say: Typically not covered: accidents, abuse, modifications and minor defects.

lines.text: A buyback isn't a full refund. Hypothetical California example: a $50,000 car first repaired at 6,000 miles loses a $2,500 usage offset.
lines.say: A buyback isn't a full refund. Hypothetically, in California, a fifty-thousand-dollar car first repaired at six thousand miles loses a two-thousand-five-hundred-dollar usage offset.

lines.text: Used car with a written warranty? Federal Magnuson-Moss law lets you sue if it's broken. Sold 'as is'? It doesn't help.
lines.say: Used car with a written warranty? The federal Magnuson-Moss Act lets you sue if it's broken.

lines.text: In California, buyers who win can recover reasonable attorney fees from the maker.
lines.say: In California, buyers who win can recover reasonable attorney fees from the maker.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Most states have no lemon law for used cars
post.ig:
Most states have no lemon law just for used cars.
About 10 states have used-car lemon laws, including New York and Massachusetts.
All 50 states cover new cars: in California, 4 repair tries (2 for safety defects) or 30+ days in the shop within 18 months/18,000 miles presumes a lemon.
A buyback isn't a full refund: California subtracts a usage offset (hypothetical: $2,500 on a $50,000 car first repaired at 6,000 miles).
Sources: CA Civil Code 1793.22, CT Office of Legislative Research, FTC.
